statement: Matchsticks build figures of squares in 2 rows. Figure 1 is a column of 2 squares, one above the other, using 7 matchsticks. Figure 2 has 2 such columns and uses 12. Each new figure adds one more column of 2 squares on the right. How many matchsticks are in Figure 10?

choices.misconception: I saw that each column adds 5 matchsticks and multiplied 5 by 10, forgetting the 2 matchsticks on the left edge of the figure.
I started from the 7 matchsticks of Figure 1 and added 5 ten times instead of nine times.
I thought Figure 10 is ten copies of Figure 1, forgetting that neighbouring columns share matchsticks.
I counted 4 matchsticks for each of the 20 squares, so every shared matchstick was counted twice.

hints: How many matchsticks does each new column add?
A new column shares its left side with the figure before it. Find how many new matchsticks a column needs, then count the steps from Figure 1 to Figure 10.
Each new column adds 3 flat matchsticks and 2 upright ones, so 5. From Figure 1 to Figure 10 there are 9 new columns.

solutions.reliable: A new column of 2 squares shares its left side with the figure before it, so it needs 3 new flat matchsticks (top, middle and bottom) and 2 new upright ones on its right: 5 in all. That fits 7 and 12, and Figure 3 has 17. Figure 10 has 9 more columns than Figure 1, so it uses $7 + 9 \times 5 = 52$ matchsticks. The transferable idea: in a growing pattern, find what each step adds and count the steps carefully.
solutions.elegant: Count by direction. Figure 10 has 3 rows of flat matchsticks with 10 in each row, 30 in all, and 11 upright lines with 2 matchsticks in each, 22 in all: $30 + 22 = 52$.

whyOnTest: Growing-pattern questions test whether you can see what each step adds and count the steps without an off-by-one slip.
